symptom: On the A* walkthrough map (components/heuristic/RouteMap.tsx), the small f= score labels under the 'waiting in queue' city markers render in the browser's generic monospace font, visibly different from the city name labels above the same markers. Both are supposed to be the app's Departure Mono.
rootcause: RouteMap.module.css's .markerNote rule set `font: 600 10.5px var(--font-mono, monospace)`, but `--font-mono` is never defined anywhere in the project -- app/globals.css only defines `--font-interface`. An undefined custom property in a `var()` with a fallback resolves to the fallback, so the f= labels silently fell back to the generic `monospace` family instead of Departure Mono. The city name labels (.markerLabel) used `var(--font-interface, sans-serif)`, which is why the two text layers disagreed. The same undefined-token pattern exists in 10 other rules across components/circuit/CircuitMap.module.css and app/circuit-flow/page.module.css, but only the RouteMap note was reported.
fix: Changed .markerNote's font shorthand in components/heuristic/RouteMap.module.css from `var(--font-mono, monospace)` to `var(--font-interface, sans-serif)`, the same token .markerLabel already uses, so both text layers resolve to Departure Mono. The other 10 `var(--font-mono, ...)` usages were deliberately left untouched -- out of the requested scope.
automation_gap: jsdom (the project's only rendering environment) does not resolve CSS custom properties or apply stylesheet font rules, so a component test cannot observe the fallback. There is no CSS lint in the repo (ESLint is blocked upstream -- see CLAUDE.md). A mechanical 'every var(--font-*) must be defined' check would be the right gate, but it would immediately go red on 10 pre-existing `--font-mono` usages in the circuit pages, so it cannot land green without expanding scope to fix those too. Prevention is the documented convention instead: use the app's one font token, `--font-interface`, for text inside the SVG maps.
notes: The visible change is text-only in the DOM, so it cannot be pinned by the existing test suite. The nearest sibling token (`--font-interface`) is the app's single source for the Departure Mono stack; introducing a second font token (`--font-mono`) without defining it is what made the two label layers diverge. Fixing the 10 circuit-page usages the same way would close the recurrence class, but that is a separate visual change and was not requested.
